started:
Started {handle} without an opening.
Next: call add_slides now with only the opening, the title slide and one or two short spoken sentences. Its reply confirms the voice works and carries the authoring guide.
playable: Opening voiced in {seconds} s; the voice works. Send the user no link: they cannot open it. Write the whole walkthrough now, one to three whole slides per add_slides call; nothing plays before export, so there is no rush to send early slides. Then finish_walkthrough, fix what it names, export_walkthrough, and send the file. The authoring guide follows.
pending: Slides saved; the opening audio is still being made. Keep adding slides: export_walkthrough waits for all narration before rendering. Send the user no link.
voice_error:
Slides saved, but voicing failed: {error}
Continue with the next add_slides call. If the error repeats, stop and tell the user voicing fails on this machine, with the error; `talktrack doctor` diagnoses it. A silent video is no use.
finished:
Finished: {slides} slides, {duration}.
Next: fix the problems listed below with revise_slide, then call export_walkthrough and send the user the file it saves. Send no link.
finished_fix:
Finished: {slides} slides, {duration}.
Not ready to export yet: the findings below name slides {fix}. Fix each with revise_slide now; its reply re-checks the slide, and for a layout finding (text_too_small, overflow, drawing_overlap) preview_slides on that slide draws it again. No need to finish again. Once they are fixed, call export_walkthrough and send the user the file it saves. Send no link.
loading: The voice model is not ready yet: {status}. Send the opening with add_slides anyway; that reply may take longer.
guide_send_link: The user receives this walkthrough as a video file, not a link: write it all, finish, fix, export, then send the file.
guide_tell_user: **Export and send:** call `export_walkthrough`, then attach the file it saves in your message to the user, with a line or two on what it covers. No link; don't repeat the script.
alike: Slides {ids} in a row look alike ({look}); pictures of them follow when they could be drawn. Before you tell the user, give one of them a different look with revise_slide: takeaways beside the visual with `.side`, a second visual with `.pair`, `.full`, or another kind of visual. Keep a run only if it is one sequence the viewer should read as such.
playlist_created:
Playlist `{title}`: {count} walkthroughs, {duration}. Id: {id}
The user cannot open links. Call export_walkthrough with handle {id} and format html, then send them the file it saves.
